The exceptions help locate the boundary: a model can express a useful target while producing an invalid serialization, or derive a payment route while a conflicting call declares bankruptcy. exact_passage: The observations fit two established results. Jehiel and Moldovanu show that negative externalities among potential buyers can delay a sale under complete information, because what a party will pay depends on who would otherwise obtain the object~\cite{jehiel1995delay}. Our holders are in a stronger version of that position, since the seller itself will pay rent to the buyer. They also tie their result to Rubinstein's point that the cost of rejecting an offer determines the outcome~\cite{rubinstein1982perfect}, and a holder short of cash has a high cost of waiting. Shleifer and Vishny show that a distressed seller receives less than an asset's value in best use when its natural buyers are constrained~\cite{shleifer1992liquidation,shleifer2011firesales}. Here the natural buyer of a completing deed is a single rival. Even so, three of the four systems mostly sold above list price when short of cash, and the low prices came from Opus. We test neither theory. They suggest that this behavior is what bargaining under externalities and cash constraints tends to produce, and that it is not peculiar to these systems.
issue: A below-list cutoff is not a fair-value or forced-sale measure; the constrained-natural-buyer mechanism is not tested.
proposed_resolution: Use fire-sale literature only as conceptual context with the mismatch stated, or omit it. Do not call above-list sales evidence against its prediction.
verification_scope: primary AEA abstract directly read; source theory not empirically tested here

exact_passage: A coherent reading is that the agents apply a categorical rule, roughly ``do not hand a rival a monopoly cheaply'', and then bargain over price with a generic routine. That reading matches the controlled two-party finding that LLM negotiators can model a counterparty accurately while their final prices follow opening anchors and local adjustment~\cite{cosentino2026counterparty}. Our setting is uncontrolled and multi-player, so it cannot test that mechanism. It does show the same separation between knowing what matters to the other side and pricing it consistently, in complete games with real consequences. We describe this as strategic attention. Strategic effectiveness would require a value reference for each decision, which this cohort lacks.
